module

public import FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Composite

@[expose] public section

/-!
# Sierpiński numbers

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Sierpiński number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierpi%C5%84ski_number)
- [Si60] Sierpiński, W., Elementary Theory of Numbers. Państwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe,
  Warsaw (1960).

A positive odd integer $k$ is a *Sierpiński number* if $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ is composite for all
natural numbers $n$.
-/

namespace Nat

/--
A positive odd integer $k$ is a
[Sierpiński number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierpi%C5%84ski_number) if $k \cdot 2^n + 1$
is composite for all natural numbers $n$. In other words, every member of the set
$\{k \cdot 2^n + 1 : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is composite.
-/
def IsSierpinskiNumber (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ¬ 2 ∣ k ∧ ∀ n, (k * 2 ^ n + 1).Composite

end Nat

findings.description: The module bibliography, lines 27–28, identifies [Si60] as Sierpiński's Elementary Theory of Numbers, Warsaw (1960). The Warsaw book was published in 1964. The 1960 reference for the Sierpiński-number result is instead the article “Sur un problème concernant les nombres k·2^n+1.” This is a bibliographic error only; Nat.IsSierpinskiNumber has the correct mathematical meaning.
findings.source_evidence: The bibliography entry https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Si60 identifies the 1960 article, and Filaseta–Finch–Kozek, https://people.math.sc.edu/filaseta/papers/SierpinskiEtCoPapNew.pdf, reference [12], gives Elem. Math. 15 (1960), 73–74. Open Library's record https://openlibrary.org/books/OL5960965M.json dates Elementary theory of numbers, Państwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe, Warszawa, to 1964; the Internet Archive catalog agrees.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace [Si60] with: Sierpiński, W., “Sur un problème concernant les nombres k·2^n+1,” Elem. Math. 15 (1960), 73–74. Alternatively, if the book is intended, correct its year to 1964 and rename the citation key accordingly. The same bibliographic correction can be propagated to the two consumer files.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses ¬ 2 ∣ k without an explicit positivity hypothesis and includes exponent n = 0. The PrimePages and FFK definitions explicitly require positive odd k and positive exponents. Erdős Problem 1113 also phrases compositeness as absence of primality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For natural k, ¬ 2 ∣ k is equivalent to 0 < k ∧ Odd k. Under the positive-exponent condition, k = 1 is excluded because 1·2^1+1 = 3 is prime. Thus k > 1, and the extra n = 0 term k+1 is even and at least 4, hence composite. Conversely, the all-exponents condition restricts to positive exponents. Positivity also makes every term greater than 1, so Composite and nonprimality agree here. Both source-characterization equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The consumer formalizes second-smallest as the least Sierpiński number having some smaller Sierpiński number; the predicate under IsLeast does not explicitly require a unique smaller element.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any predicate P on ℕ, IsLeast {k | P k ∧ ∃ b, P b ∧ b < k} a is equivalent to P a ∧ ∃! b, P b ∧ b < a. If two distinct P-elements lie below a, the larger is itself a nonminimal P-element below a, contradicting leastness. Conversely, a nonminimal P-element below a would supply two distinct P-elements below a, contradicting uniqueness. This general equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: FFK's Conjecture 3 says that a Sierpiński number which is not a perfect power has its smallest prime divisor bounded as the exponent tends to infinity. Lean instead states the disjunction of being a perfect power and possessing a finite prime covering set for all exponents.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite covering set bounds every smallest prime divisor by its largest prime. Conversely, an eventual bound yields a covering set consisting of the primes up to that bound together with one prime divisor for each of the finitely many exceptional initial terms. All terms are greater than 1, so these divisors exist. The disjunction is classically equivalent to the implication under the non-perfect-power hypothesis. FFK's allowance of power base 1 is harmless because 1 is not a Sierpiński number. The covering/boundedness equivalence, the full disjunction/conditional equivalence, and the base-1 equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/use_sites.lean.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalizations found. Checked the sole definition, its Composite dependency, Mathlib conventions and homonyms, and all seven theorem use sites in the Wikipedia and Erdős 1113 files. Boundary tests exclude 0, 1, every even number, and small odd nonexamples; a proved 78557 witness establishes nonvacuity. Also proved that adding n = 0 does not change finite-cover existence for odd k. Both scratch files compile without errors; the principal equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependencies. Current source statuses agree with the consumer tags. No repository files were edited.
